messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode of care described below. A three-character category is one capital letter followed by exactly two digits, for example J44.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 49-year-old female of Asian descent

Chief Complaint: Burning with urination, frequency, and sensation of incomplete bladder emptying

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with complicated cystitis with sepsis and diagnosed with multiple urinary bladder masses. She underwent bladder mass resection, and pathology showed no evidence of malignancy. Prednisone and mirabegron were prescribed for overactive bladder. The patient developed right-sided abdominal pain, elevated lipase, and amylase levels, mild left hydronephrosis, and underwent bone marrow biopsy; results showed mild T-cell lymphocytosis and eosinophilia with normocellular marrow. The patient was given imatinib, which was stopped due to side effects.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Medications:
None

Follow-Up Care:
Follow-up recommended with the primary care physician for review of biopsy results and further management plan.

Reply with the three characters only.

text:
Principal diagnosis: the admission was for complicated cystitis with sepsis, with multiple bladder masses that were resected and showed no malignancy. Eosinophilia was found, and prednisone was given. The picture may be eosinophilic cystitis, which codes to N30.8 (other cystitis) under N30. Sepsis would be coded as A41, but the principal diagnosis is the cystitis. Under ICD-10-AM sequencing, the underlying localized infection is usually coded first, and sepsis A41 is often sequenced as principal when it is present on admission. The summary lists the reason for admission as "complicated cystitis with sepsis", so the choice is between N30 and A41. Imatinib and the bone marrow biopsy point to a work-up for hypereosinophilic syndrome, and the bladder masses suggest eosinophilic cystitis. I chose N30.

N30
